science.summary: Two observers can start with the same description of a quantum system, follow the same probability rules and still disagree about the chance of the same outcome—even while being certain of each other's assessments.

science.title: Meta-compass: An on-chip toolkit for visualizing optical spectrum and polarization
science.summary: A ruler turns length into a position on a scale. A thermometer converts temperature into the height of a liquid column. In each case, a physical quantity becomes easier to read because an instrument gives it a visible reference. We wanted to bring the same idea to light, whose properties are usually measured with separate optical components and then interpreted through additional data processing.

science.title: NASA, European sea level satellite prepped for new role
science.summary: As of Oct. 30, the Sentinel-6B satellite has been calibrated to serve as the world's go-to data source on sea level rise. The satellite has now passed all its initial system checks to ensure that its data meet the strictest quality and accuracy standards. In January, it will become the reference satellite that other sea-level missions use to calibrate their data.

science.title: Researchers count kinetochore proteins in living cells using an improved fluorescence-based method
science.summary: Accurate division of genetic material is critical for life and growth, and key to this is a protein structure called the kinetochore. Without this structure, the genetic material cannot be segregated equally into two daughter cells. science.title: House Democrats promise a US return to global climate talks
science.summary: A new House majority can push climate policy, but a full US return remains uncertain.

science.title: Team extends a qubit's lifetime, correcting errors without measuring them
science.summary: Quantum technologies, devices that can process, store or collect information leveraging the laws of quantum mechanics, could potentially outperform their classical counterparts on some tasks. Yet these devices are highly sensitive to changes or disturbances in their surrounding environment, which can disrupt quantum effects and lead to errors.

science.title: New theoretical framework free of ghostlike instabilities expands the possibilities of symmetry in particle physics
science.summary: Elementary particles and the forces governing their interactions are described by relativistic quantum field theory, in which symmetry serves as a fundamental guiding principle. For more than half a century, the possible symmetries of such theories were believed to be restricted by the Coleman–Mandula theorem and its supersymmetric extension, the Haag–Łopuszański–Sohnius theorem.

science.title: Humpback whale snot unlocks whole-genome sequencing without invasive sampling
science.summary: New research from the University of St Andrews, in collaboration with the University of Copenhagen, the North Coast Cetacean Society and Fisheries and Oceans Canada, has sequenced a whole whale genome using samples of "whale snot" collected by small drones off the coast of British Columbia—a world first.

science.title: Baby, she's back: SpaceX catches a Starship from orbit for first time
science.summary: SpaceX brought back its Starship rocket's second stage today for a first-ever midair capture at its launch pad, capping a record-setting orbital flight test.

science.summary: Researchers at the University of Osaka have discovered a remarkable quantum state forming at the boundary between a one-atom-thick material and a metal. science.title: Tigers, zebras, quantum dots: Nanoparticles assemble into patterns
science.summary: Forget about how the zebra got its stripes. For a group of Cornell engineers, an equally important question is: What drives the formation of such eye-catching patterns?

science.summary: Nature, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03772-yFear of failure can cause researchers to stay within their comfort zone, impacting innovation, argues Nessa Carey.

science.summary: Texas A&M University researchers have developed a process that converts biomass into renewable fuels and chemicals. Dr. Mark Holtzapple, professor in the Artie McFerrin Department of Chemical Engineering, aims to make producing these products more efficient and affordable by using microorganisms to break down plant material.

science.summary: Researchers from the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology (OIST) have created a spin-based microwave amplifier that operates near absolute zero, boosting signals by more than 1,000-fold while adding noise close to the bare minimum required by the laws of physics. science.title: Measurements reveal link between quantum spin and sound-carrying vibrations in an ultrathin semiconductor
science.summary: Researchers at the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering and Auburn University have achieved a scientific first: They measured atomic vibrations that carry heat and sound waves, and connected them to a quantum property called spin, which is a way of characterizing a subatomic particle's built-in magnetism.

science.title: Chiral electronics: Researchers discover a disruptive interlayer in a promising material system
science.summary: Antiferromagnets are regarded as important materials for next-generation electronics. It is difficult, however, to accurately measure some of their properties. science.summary: The slow-moving lava of an effusive volcanic eruption can transform a landscape. But escaping gases, cloud cover, accessibility issues and limited local resources can make monitoring the development of a flow field dangerous and difficult.
